quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: The middle of the lane often has an oily strip. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it rains.
Ride only on the oily strip because it gives better grip.
Avoid the entire center of the lane.
Do not worry about oil or other items in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it rains.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks collects in the center of each lane. On dry roads, this strip usually has enough grip for a motorcycle. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push the handgrip on the side you want to turn. Push the opposite handgrip to return to your original direction after you clear the hazard.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the back of the group.
Beside the leader.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front of the group, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without forcing inexperienced riders to lead.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both at the same time and use extra braking power.
Do both at the same time, but focus mainly on swerving.
Do neither action.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: You need good grip to swerve safely, so do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, what formation should you use?

options.text: Staggered formation.
Pyramid formation.
Single-file line.
Row of pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file line.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation works best for two-wheel motorcycles, but three-wheel motorcycles are too wide for this. Riders on three-wheel motorcycles should travel in a single-file line.

questions.question: When you accelerate, what happens to a sidecar attached to your motorcycle?

options.text: It feels like it is falling behind.
It feels like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.
It vibrates out of control.
It makes acceleration feel faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It feels like it is falling behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to your motorcycle. Because of its inertia, it feels like it is falling behind when you speed up.

questions.question: When you park a motorcycle next to a curb, how should you position it?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the parking space so drivers can see the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking next to a curb, position your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle by touching your rear wheel to the curb.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn both your head and shoulders.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Use only your mirrors.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best formation?

options.text: Pairs.
Staggered formation.
Single-file line.
Pyramid formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Switch to single-file when turning, riding through curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket when it is warm outside?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take breaks to remove it and cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are made to keep you cool even in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are made to keep you cool even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: In warm weather, a riding jacket helps prevent dehydration and provides protection. Many jackets are designed to protect riders while keeping them cool in warm conditions.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time.
Always brake first, then swerve.
Use only the brakes instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you must brake and swerve, do them separately. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, what should a rider do?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean away from the motorcycle and the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while your body leans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: For normal turns, lean with your motorcycle. For slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.

questions.question: When a group exits a highway, which riding formation should be used?

options.text: Staggered
Single-file
Paired up
Three across a lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Groups usually ride in a staggered formation, but should switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: What must an eye or face shield do to be effective?

options.text: Fasten securely to your head.
Block all air from passing through.
Not allow eyeglasses underneath.
Limit your side vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely to your head.
questions.explanation: An effective eye or face shield must fasten securely. It should also be scratch-free, protect against impact, allow clear side vision, let air through to prevent fogging, and fit over eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you from behind, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the center.
On the left side.
On the right side.
Anywhere in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. This discourages the passing driver from re-entering your lane too early.

questions.question: In Oregon, is riding two motorcycles side by side in one lane allowed?

options.text: No, it is illegal.
No, it is illegal when other vehicles are near.
Yes, but it is not recommended.
Yes, but only when there is heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, but it is not recommended.
questions.explanation: In Oregon, motorcycles can legally ride two abreast in one lane. However, this is unsafe and not recommended.

questions.question: In traffic, how much stopping distance do motorcycles need compared to cars?

options.text: Much less distance.
Less distance.
The same distance.
More distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same distance.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as cars in traffic.

questions.question: When a group enters a highway or curve, how should they ride?

options.text: Single-file.
In a staggered formation.
In pairs.
On the far right of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: Groups usually ride in a staggered formation, but should switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you move?

options.text: Only your head.
Your head and shoulders.
Only your shoulders.
Your entire body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only your head.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn to where you want to go. Move only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Why should you not move to the far side of your lane when being passed?

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too early.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The near side of the lane is safer.
The wind blast from the passing vehicle is stronger on the far side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Do not ride on the far side of your lane when being passed. This may tempt the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through a turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level.

questions.question: The center portion of a lane usually contains an oily strip. This part of the lane is:

options.text: Never safe for motorcyclists.
Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny outside.
Always safe, no matter the weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of a traffic lane. This area is usually safe for motorcycles unless the road is wet. The oily strip is about two feet wide, so you can often ride around it and still stay in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: Where should a load be placed?

options.text: As low as possible
As high as possible
Behind the rear axle
On one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them in saddlebags. Do not place loads high on a sissy bar or frame. High loads raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and change its balance. Always distribute loads equally on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: Riding on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be seen easily.
Is not recommended because drivers seldom use their side mirrors and may not see you.
Is recommended because a passenger in the vehicle may tell the driver that you are there.
Is illegal because you have to ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers seldom use their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center portion of the lane where the driver can see you in the rearview mirror.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Speed up.
Reduce their speed.
Move their shoulders to match the angle of the turn.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed.
questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down. Release the throttle and use the brakes if needed.
